newsitem.title: ANGOLA: Angolan rivals struggle on over diamond area.
newsitem.headline: Angolan rivals struggle on over diamond area.

text.p: Angola's government has accused the former rebel UNITA movement of retaking two towns in the northeast diamond area, causing more tension between rivals who agreed to peace in 1994 after 20 years of war.
In recent weeks UNITA has seized back several towns it lost in skirmishes in May and June when the government tried to extend its control over the entire countryside.
In fresh accusations over fighting in the diamond-rich Lunda Norte province, state radio said on Tuesday UNITA had taken the towns of Maquesse and Caxinagagi, but gave no estimates of casualties.
The U.N. Observer Mission overseeing the final stages of a 1994 peace treaty said it was trying to verify the claims.
"We have received these reports from the government," a U.N. official said. "We are sending a team to the area to try to verify these claims now."
UNITA is officially part of a power-sharing government with the ruling MPLA and over 60 of its members are in parliament, but it still holds vast areas of rural Angola.
It has been accused by the government and others of maintaining an army of thousands.
The World Food Programme (WFP) also reported that 500 people arrived in Saurimo town, about 200 km (125 miles) southwest of where clashes were reported, saying they had fled armed troop movements.
"Our office in Saurimo says these people say they are coming into the city because of a large-scale movement of armed troops," a WFP official told Reuters.
The displaced people did not say if the armed soldiers were from UNITA or the government.
Military analysts said this government offensive into the UNITA-held areas in the northeast was the largest military operation since the peace accord was signed.
